newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia woos investors with political risk credits.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia woos investors with political risk credits.

text.p: Bosnia is offering foreign investors financial protection against the risk of war and political instability in a bid to restore confidence in the country's shattered economy, a government official said on Thursday.

With support from the World Bank, the Bosnian government has established an Investment Guarantee Agency (IGA) to offer guarantees to foreign investors providing credits to local industries, Lamija Kosaric, the agency's director, said.
"This ensures that a guarantee holder is fully protected by an independent and strong financial source outside Bosnia-Herzegovina," Kosaric said.

The Bosnian government hopes the investment protection scheme will woo foreign direct investors and lessen the country's dependence on international aid to rebuild its infrastructure devastated by a 43-month civil war that ended over a year ago.

Each IGA guarantee will be backed by an irrevocable standby letter of credit from ING Bank of the Netherlands. ING currently holds $18 million in government funds set aside to cover losses stemming from IGA-identified risks.
Investors must provide credit to a production-related business in the Balkan country to qualify for the guarantees.

Coverage includes a range of political risks, including civil disturbances and a renewal of armed conflict, as well as certain government acts that could prevent a local business from repaying its credit.
The minimum guarantee is 100,000 German marks ($59,400) and the maximum is 3,000,000 marks with up to three years of coverage, she said.
The investor must annually pay the IGA three percent of the guaranteed credit amount.

The agency has already received five applications from abroad, including a construction company providing credit for local road building and bus leasing and an Italian company's credit to a Bosnian sock factory, she said.
The World Bank's Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency grants guarantees for larger and longer-term investments beyond the coverage offered by IGA.
